spec_match.rationale: The three additions were read from the explainer — two events and a read-only replacedByUserAgent property — and the index states the explainer's own position that author opt-out is deferred to future work, so a page gets the chance to adapt rather than a veto. The adaptation demo is the explainer's own example, built and working.

interactive.rationale: A probe with positive and negative controls; a working product page whose zoom lens, provenance badge, caption and colour note all react to the events; and an observability audit that reads nine properties from a real loaded image and hashes its pixels.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index frames the problem as the page furniture around an image rather than the image itself, which is the explainer's framing, and says up front that the adaptation demo simulates the replacement.

edge_cases.rationale: The three endings on one event — finished, failed, reverted — are handled and demonstrated separately, with the failure case shown to keep the lens hidden. The pixel-hash workaround handles the tainted-canvas case, which is the normal one for a CDN-hosted image.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/5076374013476864 on the index and all three concept pages, with the explainer, the HTML images section and MDN.

conformance.rationale: Six immutable assertions: the interface exists; the detection technique works (an inherited handler is found, an invented one is not); the property exists; both handlers exist; an unknown-event listener is harmless, which is what lets the adaptation code ship unbranched; and a loaded image's observable properties describe the request rather than the display.

runtime_evidence.rationale: deno task drive over all three pages in real Chrome 150: 3/3, 26 assertions. Verified: none of the three additions is present while both controls behave; the adaptation handlers correctly hide the lens, show the badge and rewrite the caption on start, keep the lens hidden on a failure ending and restore everything on a revert; and 6 of 9 observable properties would be unchanged by a swap, with the pixel hash taking 4.5ms for a 64×64 downscale. NOT verified: any real replacement — no browser here performs one, so the events are dispatched by the page and labelled as such on the page itself.

telemetry_health.rationale: Each page emits showcaseTelemetry.assert with the probe counts, each adaptation, and the observability audit's blind count.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, no raw colour literals, buttons set background and colour, 44px control minimums, and the wide tables in their own scroll containers.

accessibility.rationale: The journal is role=log with a name; the swatches are a labelled group with per-swatch titles; the sample image carries alt text describing why it is there; every adaptation is announced through aria-live as well as being visible.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: The product layout is auto-fit minmax(260px) and stacks at 360px; the image frame uses aspect-ratio so it stays square; the sample image is max-width constrained; every table scrolls in its own container.

openQuestions.title: The replacement is simulated, and no browser will fire the real events yet
openQuestions.detail: The adaptation page dispatches its own events, which exercises the handler code but not the platform. When a browser ships the feature, the same page should work unchanged — the listeners are attached with the proposed names and the handlers read replacedByUserAgent where it exists — and that is worth verifying rather than assuming, since it is the whole claim the page makes about itself.

openQuestions.title: No opt-out exists to demonstrate
openQuestions.detail: The explainer defers author hints to future work, so there is nothing for a page to say about which images may be replaced. That is a deliberate gap and the index says so — but it is also the question every author will ask first, and a fourth concept covering it will be needed the moment a mechanism is proposed.

guidanceConsulted.query: announce a state change that alters what an image shows
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: When content changes underneath a user, say so in text as well as visually — and keep the description of the content honest when the content changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The adaptation rewrites the caption and shows a provenance badge rather than only hiding a control, because a screen reader user gets nothing from a hidden zoom lens. The whole point of the page is that alt text and captions stop being true, so the demo fixes them rather than only the visual furniture.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: deno task drive asserts the caption text changes on start and is restored on revert.

guidanceConsulted.query: feature detecting an event handler on an element
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Test the reflected on… property, and test it on an element rather than on a prototype so inherited handlers count.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied, and it corrected the first version of this page: the probes originally read HTMLImageElement.prototype, which declares no event handlers at all — every handler an image has is inherited from HTMLElement — so a prototype-only check would have reported a false negative for any handler the proposal later inherits rather than declares.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: The surface list shows 0 own event handler properties on HTMLImageElement.prototype while onload is found on an element.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive product layout with an image and details
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Auto-fit two-column layouts that stack; constrain media with aspect-ratio rather than fixed heights.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The product block is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(260px, 1fr)) and the image frame uses aspect-ratio: 1, so it stays square at every width.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: responsive-check desktop + mobile on the feature.

summary: Three concepts about a proposal with no implementation, built so the argument for it is measured rather than asserted: nine observable properties read from a real image, six of which would be identical after a replacement, and exactly one — the pixels — that would differ, at the cost of a canvas read-back that fails outright for cross-origin images. Building it corrected the page's own detection technique, which was checking a prototype that declares no event handlers at all.
